Novaflow (YC S25) is the AI data analyst for biology labs. Bioinformatics data analysis is a time-consuming and expensive process for scientists. Aman Agarwal was a computational biologist and saw firsthand how his colleagues struggled to analyze their experimental results quickly due to a growing backlog of data in the lab. Despite his lab spending over $100,000 a year on data analysis, it still wasn’t enough. He realized that this process can be automated using LLMs, saving researchers time and money. He teamed up with his friend Amulya B. , who was a software engineer at Zoom, to bring this product to life. Novaflow helps scientists get instant results from their experimental data, using custom agents that plan, generate, and run analysis behind the scenes. Scientists can simply upload their data and describe their experiment in everyday language. Novaflow determines the correct workflow, processes the data, and generates publication-ready plots, providing results in minutes instead of months. As a result, researchers spend less time doing analysis, letting them focus on their experiments and speed up scientific discovery. Visit novaflowapp.com to book a call. Congrats on the launch, Aman and Amulya! 🚀 https://lnkd.in/guHqEc_q ...more ...more

Time really does fly. Last Friday, I wrapped up my ten week internship at Prudential Financial and I couldn't be more grateful for such a rewarding and fulfilling experience. This summer, I had the great opportunity of learning not only new technologies within my role, but also the foundations of various business practices surrounding Group Insurance. As a SWE intern, I shipped production observability dashboards in Dynatrace, validating payment calculations between Prudential's legacy systems and new AWS microservices my team was developing as a modernization effort for the company. I additionally developed a pipeline automating dashboard analysis using Claude's LLM API to generate reports that helped the team diagnose and resolve issues more efficiently. Beyond work with my team, I participated in Prudential's Hackathon and our group's project won 3rd place. We built a desktop background process that protects PII by scanning employee's clipboard activity as they copy text and notifying them directly whenever sensitive information has been detected. The system additionally allows for automatic redactions that preserve context before pasting information into LLMS, emails, Microsoft Teams, etc. As I step away and move into my final semester of college, I leave with a greater understanding of working on real-world technical projects in a professional setting, a greater confidence in myself in navigating and adapting to quick and complex technical environments, and a vaster curiosity for understanding the businesses of insurance and asset management. I want to give a very special thanks to my manager Archana Upadhyaya , mentor Martina McCarthy , recruiter Jessica Torres , Paula Arroyave , Akashdeep Singh , Allison Denham , William Donahue , Joshua B. , and everyone else on my team who answered my endless questions. I would also like to thank Dana Cruz (Bochna) , Cymón H. W. , Darshana Rao and the rest of the Early Talent Team for their support and efforts in ensuring we had the best and most fulfilling experience over the summer. Lastly, I would like to thank my fellow interns for making this experience beyond special. I'll definitely miss our funny and weird lunch and group chat conversations that brought us all just a little closer together. I'm excited to see what great things all of you will do next. #prudential #internship #techcareers

I am thrilled to announce that I recently completed a summer internship with Mintz & Gold LLP in Midtown Manhattan! One of my biggest takeaways was seeing firsthand the benefits of a midsize, boutique-style law firm. This style of firm creates opportunities for attorneys to work closely with each other for their clients, leading to more personal and thorough representation. During my time at the firm, I had the opportunity to conduct legal research, listen-in on team meetings and client calls, summarize dozens of documents for the partners, compile estate planning and personal injury information into spreadsheets, and contribute to a variety of other projects. More importantly, I gained a first-hand look into what it means to work in the legal profession and serve clients. The attorneys that I got to work with shared invaluable advice as I continue to build my future career in law. I would like to extend my deepest gratitude to Ms. Halle Preston, Mr. Craig Spector, Mr. Steven Mintz, and Mr. Steven W. Gold for making this summer such a meaningful experience. I am especially grateful to have been invited to return for the summer after originally joining the firm for a two week internship. As I return to Rutgers for my junior year, I’m excited to build upon what I learned this summer and see where this next chapter takes me! #Law #LegalInternship #Rutgers

5,500+ applications. 2,000+ selected builders. 60+ countries. $35K+ prize pool. 24 hours. One global winner. Somehow, it was us. At Hack-Nation ’s 6th Global AI Hackathon, AMBR placed first in every category we competed in: 🥇 1st Place — Challenge 6 🥇 1st Place — Harvard/MIT Hub 🏆 1st Place Overall — Global Winner We built AMBR: a machine-learning research platform for decoding antibiotic resistance directly from bacterial DNA. It turns reconstructed genomes into fast, traceable evidence on which antibiotics may still be effective. Rather than explain it further, here’s our live Zoom pitch rehearsal from just before the finals. :) Grateful to have built this alongside Daniel Hofmann , Tom Burkart , and Maximilian von Klinski , incredibly talented teammates who made the entire experience unforgettable. A huge thank you as well to Hack-Nation, the organizers, judges, mentors, challenge partners, and everyone behind the Harvard/MIT Hub for creating this opportunity. With the right team, you can do anything. AMBR out. 🧬 #HackNation #Hackathon #AIForScience #MachineLearning #AntimicrobialResistance

This summer, I had the incredible opportunity to take part in JPMorgan's Fellowship program with the Commercial and Investment Bank’s Risk Management division in NYC! Over the course of the program, I worked through curriculum spanning credit and market risk, building a strong foundation in topics ranging from credit risk assessment to hedging strategies. I gained an appreciation for how risk assessment is combined with judgment and cross-team communication to ensure that a bank as large and complex as JPMorgan can continue operating smoothly, day in and day out. I'm truly thankful for the mentors and peers I met along the way, who made this program such a valuable and memorable experience. Excited to bring these learnings forward!

Two months ago I walked into a hotel lobby of 30 students not knowing exactly where I fit in this industry. Last week I was leading the main attraction at an Under Armour MLB All-Star Week event in Philadelphia, feet away from players I grew up watching. It started with the IMPACT Learning Institute . Over two weeks in NYC, we sat with executives from the NFL, NBA, MLB, The Team, Excel Sports Management, Barstool Sports, and more. I moderated panels, asked questions, and built relationships with people whose careers I want to follow. Felisa ingrained three words into us: Trust, Respect, and Credibility. I have been living by them ever since. IMPACT gave me the confidence and the network. 10 Fold Entertainment , REVERE , and Under Armour gave me the chance to prove it. At the Under Armour MLB All-Star activation event, I led the HitTrax batting cage experience for 500+ kids and families and got to be a part of the energy that celebrated Philadelphia, baseball, and youth. Thank you to Felisa Israel , Nathan Leonard and the IMPACT team, Lexie King and the Revere crew, and Kasey Wolfe and Under Armour for the trust and the recognition. This is the kind of impact I want to keep making in my professional career. Photo Credits: Henry Green Raffaella Vogt
